Water first. Substrate second. 💧🌱 This is personally my favorite way to add substrate, especially for a no CO₂, no-filter aquarium. I start with about 2 cm of water, then add the substrate directly into it. The water immediately traps most of the fine particles, instead of letting a cloud of dust spread everywhere. I also don’t rinse my substrate, because I prefer to keep everything it contains rather than washing part of the fine material away. Less dust. Less mess. Nothing wasted. Just water first. 🌿 Would you try it this way? New project in collaboration with @aquasistema_es 💚 #aquarium #aquascape #aquascaping #fishtank #plantedtank

An aquarium’s filter does far more than keep the water looking clean. It continuously removes waste, circulates oxygen, and provides a home for beneficial bacteria that break down harmful toxins produced by fish and uneaten food. Without proper filtration, ammonia and other toxic compounds can quickly build up, turning a healthy aquarium into a dangerous environment for its inhabitants. A good filtration system helps maintain water quality, stabilize the ecosystem, and keep fish healthy over the long term. While decorations and lighting may catch the eye, the filter is the unseen engine that keeps the entire aquarium alive.

That surface slick (a buildup of proteins, organic waste, and micro-debris) isn't just an eyesore—it can actually affect your Betta's health. Because Bettas are labyrinth fish, they rely on breathing atmospheric air directly from the water surface. A heavy oil film acts as a barrier, reducing essential gas exchange and making it harder for them to gulp fresh oxygen comfortably. 🛒 Check out @Fzone-US for premium surface skimmer details. #aquarium #aquascape #bettafish #betta_lover #bettatok
